pairs.subject: agent-runtime-assembly
pairs.evidence: app/api/intake/[id]/message/route.ts:99 Each intake route runs one spawned engine exchange per HTTP request, with no tool-calling loop, hook chain, contributed extension or checkpoint store; a case-insensitive grep of app/api/intake and app/api/apply for plugin, checkpoint, tool_call, toolCall and subagent found nothing, so the subject's precondition (an assembled agent runtime) does not hold here.

techniques.evidence: app/api/intake/[id]/message/route.ts:198 There is no running multi-call unit to inject into. A turn that lands while another is in flight is refused by a compare-and-swap on the row, and that refusal is the technique's own fallback for this case.
app/api/intake/[id]/message/route.ts:141 The model call finishes inside the request. No remote handle outlives a turn, and nothing is polled from a model loop.

app/api/intake/[id]/message/route.ts:64 The late-bound runner is host code registered at boot to break an import edge, not contributed code. Even so, when it is missing it degrades the way an observational contribution should: the failure is logged and the round is recorded unclassified.

pairs.subject: agent-runtime-assembly
pairs.evidence: app/api/devcase/lifecycle/[id]/redesign/route.ts:58 The lifecycle routes are store transactions plus single spawned design/evaluation passes behind a human approval gate, with no hook chain, tool loop, extension surface or checkpoint mode; grep of app/api/devcase for plugin, checkpoint, tool_call, toolCall and subagent found nothing, so the subject does not govern this context.

techniques.evidence: app/api/devcase/lifecycle/[id]/redesign/route.ts:15 The redesign is one synchronous pass inside the request. The resumed lifecycle walk is a task-runner job, which job-coordination and hitl-approval govern, not a model polling remote work.

pairs.subject: agent-runtime-assembly
pairs.evidence: app/api/devcase/session/[id]/chat/route.ts:123 The candidate chat is one model call per request, stored as a transcript, with no tools, hooks, contributed code or checkpoint representation to assemble; grep of app/api/devcase for plugin, checkpoint, tool_call, toolCall and subagent found nothing, so the subject's precondition does not hold.

techniques.evidence: app/api/devcase/session/[id]/chat/route.ts:105 An interrupted exchange leaves a user turn with no reply. The work is a pure generation with no side effect that could have escaped, so by the technique's own sort it is re-issuable, not indeterminate.
app/api/devcase/session/[id]/chat/route.ts:113 Each message is its own unit with a single model call. There is no mid-unit model-call boundary for input to join.

app/api/devcase/session/[id]/chat/route.ts:134 There is no wrapping frame around a tool call. The keyless stub's reply is still labelled with its producer, which matches the technique's spirit outside its precondition.

techniques.evidence: app/features/tools/analyze/AnalyzeApi.ts:329 The poller is a UI client reading a durable task row, not a model loop holding a remote handle. The store-is-truth shape is already present, but the technique's precondition is not.

techniques.evidence: app/api/llm/config/route.ts:70 Configuration the service can write names a provider from a closed vocabulary, plus only maxTokens and timeoutS (pipeline/jobfit/llm/config.py:100-101). Key routes take network endpoints, not entry points, so no service door can name code.
